# Wiki Cell Grammars

Some cells hold a value with a fixed form. This lookup holds how a template declares that form and what the audit checks; the grammars of particular page types have lookups of their own, listed below.

**See also:** `wiki-authoring-spec` — for the readability rules and the list of every author-facing lookup.
**See also:** `wiki-surface-cell-grammars` — for the surface-link and flow-steps grammars and the Actions bullet.
**See also:** `wiki-surface-placement-cell-grammars` — for the surface bullets that place a surface.
**See also:** `wiki-sitemap-cell-grammars` — for the sitemap table's grammars and the node reference.
**See also:** `wiki-journey-cell-grammars` — for the journey stage and opportunity grammars.
**See also:** `wiki-layout-pattern-cell-grammars` — for the region, landmark and region-reference grammars.
**See also:** `wiki-entity-cell-grammars` — for the field-source, logical-type, typed-example and field-name grammars and common fields.

## Cell grammars

Some cells hold a value with a fixed form — a type from the data dictionary, a field name, a
value from a declared set — and a template says which on a `Cells:` docblock label.
`/wiki-conformance-audit` checks every such cell on a page against that form. A cell the label
does not name keeps whatever form its body comment describes, and review is its only check.

**The label.** `Cells: <address> — <grammar>; <address> — <grammar>.` An address names where
the cell sits, its parts joined by ` › `:

| Address | Names | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `<Section> › <Column>` | a column of the `##` section's table | `Data model › Type` |
| `<Section> › <Bullet> › <Column>` | a column of the table under a block bullet | `Surfaces › Actions › Kind` |
| `<Section> › <Bullet>` | a block bullet's own value | `Surfaces › Flow steps` |
| `<Section> › (label)` | the parenthetical in a step id's label, one cell per labeled line, named by the id | `Steps › (label)` |
| `<Section> › (bullets)` | each top-level bullet of the section's list, one cell per bullet | `Task flows › (bullets)` |

The two-part form names a bullet in a section the template's `Blocks:` label names, and a
column anywhere else. A bullet's value is the text after `- **<Label>** — ` up to its first
blank line, table, comment or code block, or the next `- **<Label>**` bullet; an indented
sub-bullet is part of the value. Every platform copy of the bullet (`**Actions (mobile)**`)
is read the same way. The `(label)` form reads each line of the section that opens with a
step id and ` — ` (`**S2 (system) — Poll**`); the cell's value is the parenthetical as
written, `(system)` or `()`, and empty when the label has none. The `(bullets)` form reads each
top-level `- ` line from the section's first bullet on, and the cell's value is the line's text;
lead prose before the first bullet is no cell. A column or bullet missing
from a page is the table's or the block's finding, not the cell's.

**The set is closed.** The engine holds the grammars listed here and in the lookups listed above, and a template names only these.
A grammar checks how a value is written — a link, an id, a name, a value of a stated type, a
value from a declared list — and leaves conditions and notes to prose. No grammar uses `|`, because a table row splits
on it; where a cell holds several values, `;` separates them.

- **`one-of`** — one of the values the declaration lists after the grammar name, separated by
  ` | `: `Surfaces › Actions › Kind — one-of primary | secondary | destructive | nav | view` admits
  exactly those values. Inline code around the value is allowed. On a block-bullet address,
  `None.` also passes, for a surface the bullet does not apply to; in a table column it is not a value.
- **`flow-link`** — a bullet that opens with one link to a `task-flow` page, a shared flow
  included, then ` — ` and the outcome: `[[product:flows/billing/pay-invoice]] — the user pays an
  open invoice`. The audit errors on a bullet that does not open with a link, a link to a page that is
  not a `task-flow`, and a link with no outcome.
- **`scenario-steps`** — the step references closing a test-scenario row's Scenario cell, a
  parenthesized list after the keyword `flow` or `flows`: `(flow #S1, #A2)`, a range as
  `#S1–S2`. A bare id names a step of the flow the page verifies. A feature page's e2e row
  spans several flows, so each id there carries its flow's link,
  `(flows [[product:flows/billing/pay-invoice]]#S1, [[product:flows/billing/set-invoice-due-date]]#E1)`,
  naming a flow the feature lists under its Task flows. A cell with no such list states none.
  Each id, and both ends of a range, must be one its flow defines, so a step renumbered or
  removed leaves a finding. The audit reports a list in no known form, a bare id on a page whose
  subject is not a flow, a link to a page that is not a `task-flow`, a flow the page's subject
  does not cover, and an id the flow lacks, all as warnings (`scenario-step-refs`). `scenario-e2e-spans-flows`
  also warns on a feature page's e2e row whose links name one flow only, and points to that flow's
  scenario page.
- **`step-marker`** — the parenthetical of a step id's label: empty, or `(<marker>)` with the
  marker one of `system`, `agent` or `external`. `()` is an unknown marker, not an unmarked step.

Each failure carries a reason code, `<grammar>/<reason>`, which the conformance findings file and
the surfaces graph publish; agent-kit's orchestration guide, § *Reason codes*, lists the codes.

**A pending cell.** `Pending: <name>`, in a cell whose grammar admits it, is legal only where a
row of the page's own `## Open questions` table names `<name>` verbatim in its Question cell.
That row's Owner and Resume condition say who settles it and when. A pending cell no row names is
an error, for the reason a section's `Pending:` outside a declared slot is: unbounded, it would
leave the cell's check suppressed indefinitely. A `Pending:` cell with no name after the colon is
an error too, because no row can name it.

**What stays judgment.** The audit checks a cell's form, and that what the form names exists
and suits the cell. It does not check whether a value is the right one: whether a `Leads to`
names the right destination and its condition holds, whether a step listed under `Flow steps`
really happens on that surface, whether a `Source` field means what its label shows, whether
an example was invented rather than copied — personal names and street addresses included —
or a component variant a `Consequence` names. `conformance-checks.json`'s judgment list
records these, so the verdict never claims them.
